Bask Health brings together merchant operations, patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy coordination, and commerce tools. Many of these processes involve multiple applications, structured information, business rules, and repetitive tasks. You'll help build AI-powered systems that can coordinate these steps while operating within clearly defined permissions and reliability requirements. This role focuses on developing production AI agents that use large language models, application tools, retrieval systems, and workflow orchestration to complete approved tasks. jobs.jd: About Bask Health Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place. We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform. Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality. About the Role We're looking for an Applied ML Engineer, Care Experience to develop intelligent software capabilities that improve how patients receive support and navigate ongoing care-related experiences through Bask Health 's platform. Bask Health provides the technology behind direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses, connecting patient onboarding, clinical workflows, pharmacy coordination, and ongoing patient interactions. These processes often involve communication, administrative follow-ups, operational handoffs, and coordination between multiple systems and teams. You'll help build machine learning and AI-powered features that make these experiences more consistent, efficient, and easier to manage for patients and authorized care teams. This is a hands-on applied machine learning engineering role that combines large language models, predictive modeling, backend development, and workflow automation. You'll work with approved patient-related information, application events, APIs, and model outputs to develop intelligent features that support care-related operations. Your work may include intelligent message classification, administrative request routing, AI-assisted communication, workflow prioritization, and systems that help authorized teams identify incomplete or delayed operational tasks. You'll collaborate with product managers, applied AI engineers, machine learning specialists, and clinical or pharmacy operations stakeholders to understand workflow requirements and translate them into reliable software capabilities. You'll also help evaluate model accuracy, monitor production behavior, and improve machine learning systems based on real-world performance. You'll need to understand when traditional software rules, predictive models, or large language models are most appropriate for a particular problem. Because these applications support healthcare-related workflows, accuracy, privacy, appropriate permissions, and human oversight are essential. You'll build systems that support authorized professionals and administrative processes without independently diagnosing patients, recommending treatments, prescribing medications, or making clinical decisions. This position emphasizes practical engineering, measurable improvements, and responsible deployment. You'll contribute to technical design, build production features, and continuously improve systems based on user feedback and evaluation results. We're looking for an engineer who enjoys applying machine learning to real operational challenges, understands the importance of dependable software in sensitive environments, and wants to help make ongoing care experiences easier to manage. What You'll Do Build and maintain machine learning and AI-powered capabilities that support ongoing patient care experiences. Develop intelligent systems for approved patient support and care coordination workflows. Implement machine learning models that classify and organize patient-related administrative requests. Build AI-assisted tools that help authorized teams understand and manage incoming communications. Develop routing and prioritization systems for operational tasks and support requests. Implement intelligent workflow assistance for follow-ups, status updates, and administrative coordination. Build backend services and APIs that connect ML capabilities to existing platform applications. Integrate large language models into approved care-related operational workflows. Develop structured output pipelines that convert model responses into validated application data. Build information retrieval capabilities that surface relevant approved workflow information. Implement AI-assisted summaries for authorized care and operations teams. Develop systems that help identify incomplete administrative workflows or delayed operational handoffs. Evaluate opportunities to apply predictive modeling to approved care experience use cases. Design feature engineering and data processing workflows for machine learning applications. Build automated tests for model outputs, APIs, and application behavior. Evaluate models for accuracy, relevance, consistency, and operational usefulness. Investigate incorrect classifications, unreliable responses, and unexpected model behavior. Improve model configurations, prompts, and application logic based on evaluation results. Implement human review and confirmation steps for sensitive workflows. Ensure ML-powered features respect user permissions and approved data access. Collaborate with product and operational stakeholders to define measurable success criteria. Monitor production model behavior, application errors, and workflow performance. Optimize inference latency, reliability, and operational costs. Work with backend engineers to integrate ML services into production infrastructure. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Agent Eval Platform
jobs.jd: The Role Moveworks' AI agents don't just generate text — they act. They plan, call tools, and change real state in enterprise systems on behalf of 5.5 million employees. Building agents is no longer the bottleneck. Improving them is: knowing whether a change made the agent better, why a conversation failed, and which part of the system should be fixed. You'll build the loop that makes our agents improve themselves — finding failures in real use, deciding which part of the agent harness is responsible, checking every proposed fix on cases the fixer never saw, and turning each fixed failure into a permanent test. We improve the system around the model: instructions, tool descriptions, routing, knowledge and memory. We don't train the model itself. The work is blend of ML and systems engineering. You'll decide whether a signal is trustworthy enough to act on, and build the infrastructure that produces that signal reproducibly across hundreds of customer organizations. This isn't a model-training role, and it isn't a testing role. Concretely, that means designing and building RL environments that reproduce realistic security scenarios, pipelines that generate synthetic training instances at scale , and experiments and evaluations that show what our models can actually do. Partner with researchers and security specialists across Mistral, distilling their domain expertise into reproducible environments and datasets. We inspire people to achieve great things together. Our mission is to help organizations unlock the power of inspirational communication with the first AI-native Employee Experience Platform. Our industry-leading and award-winning agentic AI communications channels - intranet, employee app and email solutions - create engaging experiences that connect and empower employees.

Headquartered in Chemnitz, Germany and New York City, with offices in Berlin, London, Sydney, Tokyo, Prague, and Minneapolis–St. Paul, our diverse team of 550+ employees supports 1,500+ customers—reaching over 14 million employees—in transforming their employee experience.
We are proud to be a Unicorn company—privately valued at over $1 billion—demonstrating strong growth, innovation, and lasting impact in our industry. Together, we’re shaping the future of workplace communication.

This is a hands-on technical role within Staffbase Build, responsible for turning specific enterprise customer needs into reliable, scalable extensions of the Staffbase platform, using its extensibility capabilities (widgets, plugins, integrations, and other platform objects). The role owns assigned customer solutions end-to-end, defining the use case with stakeholders, building and testing across the stack, deploying it, and validating it with users.

The aim is to drive adoption and stickiness of the platform, not to create one-off, standalone customer solutions. The role acts as a bridge, helping customers do what they and the platform can't do alone yet, and feeds what's learned back into shared standards and the product roadmap.

The role reports into the regional Build Leader.

What you’ll be doing

Solution Delivery

  • Owning the technical design, implementation, testing, and release of assigned custom solutions end-to-end
  • Building across the stack (customer-facing UI, backend services, and integrations with Staffbase and third-party APIs)

Customer & Stakeholder Collaboration

  • Partnering with customers, consultants and internal teams, e.g. Sales, to define and detail use cases before development. Supporting pre-sales in a technical advisory capacity, primarily during requirements discovery: join customer and Sales conversations to clarify needs, assess technical feasibility, and help scope custom solutions
  • Validating shipped solutions with users and gathering feedback afterward
  • Supporting customers in building basic solutions themselves using Staffbase-provided platform tools where appropriate, rather than defaulting to a fully bespoke build

Platform-First Engineering

  • Keeping up to date with new and evolving platform capabilities (new extensibility primitives, APIs, and platform objects) so solutions are built using the latest native capabilities rather than defaulting to more bespoke patterns
  • Applying the company's architectural, security, and compliance standards so solutions remain supportable

Pattern Capture & Product Feedback

  • Identifying reusable patterns and components arising from customer engagements; documenting and contributing them to a shared Build asset catalogue
  • Surfacing recurring, validated customer needs for consideration in the product roadmap

Craft & Team Contribution

  • Maintaining a strong quality bar (testing, code reviews, healthy CI/CD practices).
  • Participating in the Build on-call rotation to support shipped customer solutions, in line with the applicable regional on-call policy.
  • Helping bring structure and engineering standards to the team, and mentor less experienced engineers

What you need to be successful 

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, building and running production systems
  • Customer-facing technical experience (forward-deployed, solutions engineering, consulting)

jobs.title: Applied Scientist, Superconducting Digital and Cryogenic Control Electronics,Center for Quantum Computing, Physical Design and Simulation, Enabling Technologies
jobs.jd: The Amazon Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is seeking an Applied Scientist to research and design cryogenic control hardware for large-scale quantum processors, with an emphasis on superconducting digital circuits. Controlling and reading out orders of magnitude more qubits than today's systems demands rethinking where classical control lives and what technology implements it; you will design and model superconducting digital logic (e.g., single-flux-quantum-family circuits) and related cryogenic electronics, evaluate them against the wiring, power, and thermal budgets of a scaled system, and co-design control approaches with the qubit devices they serve. You will carry designs from concept through simulation, layout, design review, and fabrication handoff, and your evaluations will inform which control-electronics directions the organization invests in. Key job responsibilities • Design and simulate superconducting digital circuits and cryogenic control/readout electronics for scalable qubit control • Develop and validate Josephson-junction circuit models, timing and margin analyses, and verification methodology for superconducting digital designs • Quantify system-level trade-offs — wiring count, power dissipation at each cryogenic stage, latency, footprint — across candidate control architectures, and communicate recommendations • Co-design control interfaces with qubit-device colleagues so control electronics and quantum devices are developed as one system • Deliver design artifacts through the organization's design-request and design-review processes, including tapeout-ready layouts and verification reports • Present results internally and, where appropriate, publish in peer-reviewed venues About the team The Enabling Technologies team develops technologies and relationships facilitating scaling, including alternative quantum processor architectures, superconducting qubit device packaging, and cryogenic control device electronics. We work alongside a co-located quantum processor design team focused on current-generation devices; the two teams share design and review processes, and moving ideas between them is an explicit part of our charter. - Knowledge of cryogenic electronics more broadly: cryo-CMOS, low-temperature amplifiers and mixers, thermal and power budgeting across refrigerator stages - Experience with microwave engineering and signal integrity in dense cryogenic interconnect - jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, Startups (Codex)
jobs.jd: About the team The Applied AI Engineering team works closely with frontier startups. We are trusted advisors to, and thought partners with, startups to ensure that OpenAI’s technology is deployed safely and effectively, whilst also partnering with engineering, research, and product to turn those insights into evaluation systems, product improvements, and better model behavior. This team sits at the intersection of customer reality and model quality. We combine hands-on technical depth with strong product judgment, helping translate complex, high-value use cases into clear signals that can improve both the customer experience and the underlying systems. About the Role As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex for startups, you will help developers and founders transform how they build and ship software. You’ll combine hands-on engineering, startup experience, and compelling technical communication to help teams turn the potential of AI coding tools into practical, effective workflows. Presentations and community engagement are central to this role. You will engage developers and founders through technical talks, live demos, workshops, and programmes across the startup ecosystem, alongside targeted work with individual customers. You’ll build reusable tools and resources that extend your impact, and bring insights from developers back to OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys both hands-on building and sharing what they learn with others. You should be as excited to lead a room of developers, deliver an engaging presentation, and build relationships across the startup community as you are to explore a technical problem in code—with a focus on sustained adoption and meaningful improvements in how startups work. In this role, you will: Partner with top startups to identify where Codex can have the greatest impact on how their teams build and ship software. Design and lead technical talks, live demos, workshops, hackathons, and repeatable hands-on programmes that turn initial interest into sustained adoption. Work directly with selected customers to build Codex workflows, integrations, and automations, resolve technical blockers, and evaluate effectiveness and reliability. Turn successful approaches into reusable code examples, guides, and tools that help more startups succeed with Codex and OpenAI’s broader platform. Collaborate with account teams, developer experience, and ecosystem partners to reach developers and founders, prioritise opportunities, and drive measurable customer value. Translate customer experiences and developer feedback into actionable insights for OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams. You’ll thrive in this role if you: Have experience building at, founding, or working closely with early-stage startups, and understand the pace, ambiguity, and practical trade-offs involved. Bring strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoy building practical AI applications, integrations, and developer tools. Are an active user of Codex or other AI coding tools, with a thoughtful perspective on how they can improve software development. Are a compelling communicator who enjoys presenting, delivering live demos, and leading hands-on workshops for developers and founders. Have a talent for turning complex technical ideas into clear explanations, engaging examples, and reusable resources that help others succeed. Combine developer empathy with sound technical judgment: you can uncover what a team needs, troubleshoot problems, and help them adopt effective, reliable workflows. Bring high agency, curiosity, and end-to-end ownership, working independently while collaborating closely with colleagues and ecosystem partners. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer - (AI x Greentech) (m/f/d)
jobs.jd: Make Everything Just Work Most jobs ask you to keep the lights on. This one asks you to build the machine that keeps an entire company and its customers running. At Reonic, we’re building the AI operating system for renewable installers, with competitive pay, growth opportunities and a strong culture based on ambition, impact and ownership. And we’re doing it fast. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’re where our product meets the real world. You work hands-on with renewable energy installers and their technical teams, help them build on our API, and solve the problems that stand between them and a setup that just works. Around 80% of your time is spent with customers. The other 20% goes to making Reonic itself run the way an AI-first company should. What you'll do With our customers (~80%) Enable our API users: Work with customers’ technical teams as they build on our API and webhooks. Review their approach, answer the tricky questions and get them unblocked fast. Solve problems end to end: When something breaks, you find out why. Reproduce the issue, work with engineering on the fix and keep the customer in the loop until it’s solved. Connect Reonic to their world: Make Reonic work seamlessly with the tools our customers rely on every day, from Microsoft and Google to their CRM, accounting and automation platforms. Make customers self-sufficient: Write guides, examples and snippets that help customers help themselves. Inside Reonic (~20%) Run our AI tools: Own our Claude and ChatGPT workspaces, from access and connectors to costs. Make AI part of everyone’s job: Help colleagues build integrations, connectors and automations that save them real time. Own our IT setup: Keep our tools, devices and security running smoothly, so everyone at Reonic can do their best work from day one. What makes you a great fit Technical understanding: You’re comfortable with APIs, webhooks and authentication flows such as OAuth, and you aren’t afraid to dig into the details.
